Write the dataprep.csv template of a Where To Work project

Source: R/dataprep.R
create_dataprep_template.Rd

Writes the dataprep.csv template of a Where To Work (WTW) project: a CSV file with one column per input of the regional data preparation, and a row describing each column. Analysts replace the description row with one row per regional layer, and the ArcGIS toolbox of wtw-data-prep2 (wtw-utils) reads the file in its "Batch CSV file" mode. It is the template wtw-data-prep2's step 01 writes, and the defaults write the same file.

Usage

create_dataprep_template(
  project_dir,
  file = "dataprep/dataprep.csv",
  columns = dataprep_columns(),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

project_dir

The WTW project folder: a single folder path, under which file is written. Missing folders, project_dir included, are created. Where the project lives is each tool's own setting.

file

The file to write, as a path relative to project_dir. The default, "dataprep/dataprep.csv", is the WTW project layout wtw-data-prep2 writes. It is written as a CSV file whatever its extension.

columns

The template's columns, one of:

  • a named character vector: the names are the columns and the values their descriptions, written as one row below the column names. The default, dataprep_columns(), is wtw-data-prep2's eight columns and their descriptions. Add or drop elements for another template, for example c(dataprep_columns(), notes = "comments on the layer").

  • an unnamed character vector of column names: the file holds only the column names, with no row below them.

  • a data frame: written as it is, its names as the column names and each of its rows as a row, for a template with example or prefilled rows. Its columns must be atomic vectors (not lists).

The column names must be non-empty, not NA and all different; NA values are written as empty fields.

overwrite

A single logical. TRUE (the default) replaces an existing file, as wtw-data-prep2 does, including one an analyst has filled in; FALSE is an error if the file exists, checked before anything is written.

Value

The path of the file written, file.path(project_dir, file), invisibly. The file is written as a side effect.

Method

The template is written with utils::write.csv() (row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8"), as wtw-data-prep2 writes it: fields separated by commas; a first line of column names; then one line per row (one line of descriptions for a named vector, none for an unnamed one); column names, text and factor values in double quotes, with any double quote inside them doubled; numbers and logicals without quotes; NA as an empty field; no row names. The file is UTF-8 text without a byte order mark, so names and descriptions that are not ASCII read the same on every system; lines end with the system's line ending (CRLF on Windows, LF elsewhere), as write.csv() writes them. Values are written as they are: nothing is trimmed, checked or reordered.

Arguments are checked before anything is written, and the missing folders above file are created.

With the defaults, the file is that of wtw-data-prep2's step 01 (create_project_folder()): the same bytes, on the same system. Decisions are recorded in ADR 0023.

See also

dataprep_columns(), the default columns, and create_wtw_project_folder(), which creates the project's folders (dataprep among them).

Other wtw: create_wtw_planning_units(), create_wtw_project_folder(), dataprep_columns(), extract_wtw_natdata(), wtw_project_folders()

Examples

# wtw-data-prep2's template, in a new project's dataprep folder
project_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "wtw_dataprep")
path <- create_dataprep_template(project_dir)
readLines(path)
#> [1] "\"conversion_ready_input\",\"short_name\",\"tif_output\",\"unit\",\"stat\",\"cell_value\",\"datatype\",\"provenance\""                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
#> [2] "\"full filepath to input data\",\"10 characters or less name for variable\",\"full filepath with extension to output tif\",\"supported units: m2, ha, km2, m, km and count\",\"supported stats: mean, max, min, sum, stdev, mode and area \",\"if stat is area, provide cell value to extract\",\"supported types: raster, vector\",\"national or regional\""
utils::read.csv(path)
#>        conversion_ready_input                              short_name
#> 1 full filepath to input data 10 characters or less name for variable
#>                                   tif_output
#> 1 full filepath with extension to output tif
#>                                            unit
#> 1 supported units: m2, ha, km2, m, km and count
#>                                                          stat
#> 1 supported stats: mean, max, min, sum, stdev, mode and area 
#>                                       cell_value
#> 1 if stat is area, provide cell value to extract
#>                          datatype           provenance
#> 1 supported types: raster, vector national or regional

# The manual's two optional documentation columns added
path <- create_dataprep_template(
  project_dir,
  columns = c(
    dataprep_columns(),
    source = "full path or web address of the source data",
    notes = "notes or comments on the layer"
  )
)
names(utils::read.csv(path))
#>  [1] "conversion_ready_input" "short_name"             "tif_output"            
#>  [4] "unit"                   "stat"                   "cell_value"            
#>  [7] "datatype"               "provenance"             "source"                
#> [10] "notes"                 

# Column names only, in another file
path <- create_dataprep_template(
  project_dir,
  file = "dataprep/regional.csv", columns = names(dataprep_columns())
)
readLines(path)
#> [1] "\"conversion_ready_input\",\"short_name\",\"tif_output\",\"unit\",\"stat\",\"cell_value\",\"datatype\",\"provenance\""

# A template with a filled-in row
rows <- data.frame(
  conversion_ready_input = "C:/data/regional.gdb/wetlands",
  short_name = "WETLAND",
  tif_output = "C:/project/tifs/themes/T_REG_WETLAND.tif",
  unit = "ha", stat = NA, cell_value = NA, datatype = "vector",
  provenance = "regional"
)
path <- create_dataprep_template(project_dir, columns = rows)
readLines(path)
#> [1] "\"conversion_ready_input\",\"short_name\",\"tif_output\",\"unit\",\"stat\",\"cell_value\",\"datatype\",\"provenance\""      
#> [2] "\"C:/data/regional.gdb/wetlands\",\"WETLAND\",\"C:/project/tifs/themes/T_REG_WETLAND.tif\",\"ha\",,,\"vector\",\"regional\""
